title: Render TeX math without a browser or network
lead:
Pandoc writes TeX math as MathML. WeasyPrint does not render MathML, so a PDF
shows the flattened symbols followed by the TeX source (`Pout=G⋅PinP_{out} = ...`).
boundary:
**Not in this slice:** math in HTML beyond what the same SVG provides;
numbered equations and cross-references.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
branded-pdf renders `$...$` and `$$...$$` through LaTeX. Equations are common
in RF and test documentation.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- Math nodes in the AST are replaced with inline SVG, inline or display as
  appropriate, with the TeX source kept as accessible text.
- Results are cached by TeX source and renderer version, like diagrams.
- Without the optional renderer, a document containing math fails with an
  installation hint; `--no-math` keeps Pandoc's current output.
- A TeX error names the source file and the offending expression.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Owner approval needed first: this adds an npm dependency. Proposed: MathJax
(Apache-2.0; confirm the current package name and version) converting TeX to SVG in Node, installed by the
existing `--with-mermaid` path (rename or alias the flag to cover optional
renderers), with no browser needed. Reuse the Mermaid module's cache and
worker patterns. Size SVG text relative to the surrounding font size.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `python3 test_quire.py`
- `python3 test_render_integration.py` with the optional runtime.
- Real build with inline and display equations; report how they render.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: No commit unless the owner asks.
